title: Single-change-point energy for causal structure adaptation under noisy interventions
classification: isolated synthetic development; no protected native first-use
run_stage: PRIMARY NOT YET EXECUTED AS OF PREREG COMMIT
hypothesis: A single-change-point energy formulation can retain old causal knowledge under noisy observations while learning changed causal relations, beating fixed-hazard, 16-observation window, and full-history controls given identical interventions. A mathematically equivalent conventional Bayesian reference must produce matching predictions; energy-specific distinctiveness is not implied.
method: Exact normalized negative log-likelihood energies for 40 signed XOR3 familiar and 120 generated XOR3+AND2 composite rules; latent one-change boundary over 8..39 witnessed steps, no privileged boundary marker; posterior over change points; deterministic SHA256 source streams.
source: synthetic self-authored six-bit intervention worlds generated inside pinned experiment.py; no external or protected dataset
source_partition: 64 action combinations per world; independently SHA256-shuffled 24 old and 16 challenge observations, 12 disjoint held actions. Evaluator-only truth and noise. Old prefix is not flagged as a known phase to policies.
information_actions_capacity: All five policies receive identical 40 observed action-outcome records and use the same finite 160-rule representational grammar. The single-change prior is part of tested structural bias; results must not be called an energy-specific advantage.
decision_rule: For held ground-truth causal bit, predict 1 only when P(bit=1)>0.5+1e-12. A change alarm is posterior probability of any switch >0.5 on the 40th witnessed action.

predeclared_gates.novel_gain_over_strongest: cp_energy >=3 percentage points over highest held accuracy among fixed_hazard, recent16, full_history on novel_change
predeclared_gates.familiar_gain_over_strongest: cp_energy >=3 percentage points over highest held accuracy among fixed_hazard, recent16, full_history on familiar_switch
predeclared_gates.stationary_retention: cp_energy accuracy >=95% and within 1 percentage point of full_history stationary accuracy
predeclared_gates.exact_energy_bayes_parity: Maximum posterior held probability and change alarm difference <=1e-10
predeclared_gates.energy_distinctive: Must demonstrate an energy-specific advantage; exact Bayes equivalence precludes this in this formulation (frozen false).

classification_logic: DEVELOPMENT_GO only if all gates are true; otherwise DEVELOPMENT_NO_GO; no scientific pass or promotion even with development success.
timing_policy: Record local component and whole run times descriptively, but do not claim wall-clock/whole-process speedup from alternative Python implementations. No arbitrary cross-platform speed or cost superiority claim.
stop_policy: Run exactly this frozen primary configuration once. On NO_GO, stop this candidate rather than sweeping consumed seeds or adjusting thresholds. Subsequent mechanisms need new independent source and prereg.
notes: ENERGY-32 measured 15/80 paired false alarms and no held advantage; ENERGY-33 tests structural one-change Bayesian inference, not a tuned repeat threshold. Smoke on seed 99013 was run before prereg and is excluded from primary.
